body:
### Summary

Apparently `implementation_name` filter in `tool.uv.environment` is either doesn't work or it still allows filtered out wheels to be written to lockfile.

Steps to reproduce:
1. `uv init --python 3.11 .` (3.11 is important since it has pypy wheels).
2. `uv add numpy`
3. `git add . && git commit -m "update"`
4. In `pyproject.toml` add this to limit environments to 3 platforms and use cpython only.

```toml
[tool.uv]
environments = [
    # macOS on Apple Silicon (ARM)
    "implementation_name == 'cpython' and sys_platform == 'darwin' and platform_machine == 'arm64'",
    # Linux on x86_64 (Intel/AMD)
    "implementation_name == 'cpython' and sys_platform == 'linux' and platform_machine == 'x86_64'",
    # Windows on x86_64 (Intel/AMD)
    "implementation_name == 'cpython' and sys_platform == 'win32' and platform_machine == 'AMD64'",
]
```

5. `uv lock`
6. `git diff -- uv.lock`
7. Expected: platform and implementation filters to work - intel macos and pypy wheels to get removed from lockfile.
8. Result: only intel macos wheels are filtered, pypy wheels stay (e.g. `numpy-2.4.6-pp311-pypy311_pp73-macosx_11_0_arm64.whl`).


### Platform

Ubuntu 26.04

### Version

uv 0.13.8 (Homebrew 2026-11-12 x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu)

### Python version

-
title: `implementation_name` filter doesn't work in `environment`
